comments.content: `mp_guess_lang_from_filename()` unconditionally resets `*forced` to `false` (and `*hearing_impaired` too) before parsing, so passing `&nt->forced_track` clobbers the `TRACK_FORCED` flag that was just propagated to the new track through `flags` a few lines above. For example, `sub-add foo.srt forced` followed by `sub-reload`/`track-reload` silently loses the forced marking because `foo.srt` has no `forced` tag in its name. Use a local bool and OR it into the field instead (applies analogously to `hearing_impaired_track`), e.g. `bool guessed_forced = false; ... &guessed_forced); nt->forced_track |= guessed_forced;`.

comments.content: Only one tag segment can ever be consumed, because `checked_tag` is set on the first match. Now that "forced" is also a tag, filenames with multiple tags are mis-parsed: for `foo.en.hi.forced.srt` the rightmost tag ("forced") is consumed, then the next segment "hi" falls through to language detection and is returned as the language (lang="hi", hearing_impaired=false) instead of lang="en", hi=true; the reverse order `foo.en.forced.hi.srt` consumes "hi" first and then loses the forced flag and returns no language. Consider driving tag consumption from a {tag, flag} table and consuming all consecutive tag segments (e.g. drop the one-shot `checked_tag` guard) instead of collapsing both flags into a single pass.
